**Checking sign-in on load**

`src/app/provider.tsx` wraps the whole app in `AppProvider`, and inside it sits `AuthLoader`. `AuthLoader` comes from `react-query-auth`'s `configureAuth(authConfig)` in `src/lib/auth.tsx`. On mount it runs the `userFn`, which is `getUser`. That calls `GET /auth/me` through the shared axios client. The browser sends the session cookie because `withCredentials` is set. While the request is pending, `AuthLoader` shows a full-screen spinner (`renderLoading` in `provider.tsx`). The result is cached in TanStack Query. `useUser()` then returns it, so `user.data` is the signed-in user, or empty if `/auth/me` failed.

Routes use that result in `ProtectedRoute`, also in `src/lib/auth.tsx` and used in `src/app/router.tsx`. If `user.data` is missing, it redirects to the login page. The redirect uses `paths.auth.login.getHref(location.pathname)` from `src/config/paths`, so the user returns to the page they wanted.

**When a request returns 401**

`src/lib/api-client.ts` creates the axios instance `api` with a response interceptor. On any failed response it first pushes an error toast through `useNotifications`, using the server's `message` or else the axios error message. If the status is 401, it then sets `window.location.href` to the login path with a `redirectTo` value. This is a full page navigation, not a router navigation. After that it rejects the promise, so callers still see the error.

One quirk is in the `redirectTo` logic. It builds an empty `URLSearchParams()` and reads `redirectTo` from that, so `get('redirectTo')` is always null. The value therefore always falls back to `window.location.pathname`. The `||` branch is dead code, though the end result is still the current page.

Because `/auth/me` goes through the same client, a signed-out visitor's initial check also returns 401. That shows an error toast and triggers the redirect to login, even when the visitor is on a public page like the landing page. I did not trace what happens on the login page itself, so I can't say whether this loops or is handled elsewhere.
